texts: Arabica beans contain about 1.2% caffeine while Robusta has nearly double at 2.2% — yet specialty coffee exclusively uses Arabica because the lower caffeine creates a smoother, more complex flavor, proving more stimulants don't equal better taste.

Tea leaves actually contain more caffeine by weight than coffee beans, but a brewed cup of tea has far less caffeine than coffee — because you use only 2-3 grams of tea versus 15 grams of coffee per cup, making the leaf technically more potent but brewed weaker.

Finland consumes roughly 12 kilograms of coffee per person annually — nearly four times more than Americans and ten times more than Italians — making the icy Nordic country the world's biggest coffee consumer despite having no native coffee plants.
